Five electric pianos, five ways of making a note: a struck **tine**, a struck **reed**, a struck **string** held on an anvil,
real **piano strings**, and a plucked reed. Each is rebuilt here as a small physical model with its controls as on the real
instrument. Facts come from the Wikipedia articles listed under Works Cited (read 2026-11-26). The service manuals were not read for these pages, so control legends and places that Wikipedia does not give are marked unverified.

## The instruments

| Instrument | How it makes a note |
|---|---|
| [Fender Rhodes Mark I Stage 73](intro-rhodes.qmd) | Hammer hits a **tine** + tonebar; magnetic pickup |
| [Wurlitzer 200A](intro-wurlitzer.qmd) | Felt hammer hits a **reed**; electrostatic pickup |
| [Hohner Clavinet D6](intro-clavinet.qmd) | Pad drives a **string** onto an anvil; two magnetic pickups |
| [Yamaha CP-70](intro-cp70.qmd) | Piano hammers hit **strings**; piezo pickups, no soundboard |
| [Hohner Pianet N](intro-pianet.qmd) | A pad lets go of a **reed**; capacitance pickup (N) |

**How to use it.** Pick an instrument and a riff and press **▶ Play**, or play the keys. **Panel** shows the real controls;
**Simple** shows every one as a slider, marked *on the panel*, *inside* (a service adjustment) or *this page's*.
**Turn into it** moves the sound to another instrument and lists every setting:
<span class="epc-tag epc-exact">the same</span>, <span class="epc-tag epc-approx">close</span> or
<span class="epc-tag epc-lost">lost</span>.

## How each one is modelled

- **Rhodes:** the tine's motion is a few decaying vibrations (its fundamental, the tonebar's, and two short, high bending modes:
  the bell). The pickup's magnetic field is strongest in the middle, so the output bends when the tine swings far: hit harder,
  or set the tine near the pickup's centre, and the tone gets **bark**.
- **Wurlitzer and Pianet:** a reed swinging nearer and further from a charged plate. The change is not the same on both sides,
  so loud notes gain even harmonics. The Wurlitzer's amplifier adds more.
- **Clavinet:** a string's harmonics, read by a pickup at one place along it. A pickup near the end hears more high harmonics.
  Two pickups together, or one reversed against the other, add or cancel harmonics. The tabs are filters.
- **CP-70:** two or three slightly mistuned strings per note, with sharpened overtones (stiff, short bass strings), and a pickup
  under the bridge instead of a soundboard.
- After the notes: amplifier drive, EQ, speaker, tremolo (on the Suitcase it pans left and right), volume.

All of the numbers are this page's choices, not measurements.

## Famous tracks

### Rhodes

### "Riders on the Storm" (The Doors)

[▶ The Doors - Riders on the Storm (Official Audio)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7G2-FPlvY58) on YouTube (The Doors).

Ray Manzarek played a Mark I Stage 73 in the studio (Wikipedia). Soft, rainy chords and a jazzy line, with no bark.

<div class="ik-step" data-set="{&quot;model&quot;:&quot;rhodes&quot;,&quot;voice&quot;:6,&quot;hard&quot;:3,&quot;bass&quot;:6,&quot;drive&quot;:1}" data-riff="ballad">

**Starting setting** (Rhodes): voice 6, hard 3, bass 6, drive 1. Then change it until it sounds like the record to you.

</div>

### "Angela (Theme from Taxi)" (Bob James)

[▶ Angela (Theme From Taxi)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1RCKWBFt9MU) on YouTube (Bob James - Topic).

Wikipedia names it among Rhodes recordings. A bell-like melody over chords: the tine's attack is the point.

<div class="ik-step" data-set="{&quot;model&quot;:&quot;suitcase&quot;,&quot;vib&quot;:3,&quot;rate&quot;:3,&quot;hard&quot;:7}" data-riff="ballad">

</div>

### "Just the Way You Are" (Billy Joel)

[▶ Billy Joel - Just the Way You Are (Official Audio)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HaA3YZ6QdJU) on YouTube (billyjoelVEVO).

Wikipedia does not name this song; it is widely called a Rhodes record (unverified). Soft chords with a slow, gentle movement.

<div class="ik-step" data-set="{&quot;model&quot;:&quot;suitcase&quot;,&quot;vib&quot;:4,&quot;rate&quot;:2.5,&quot;hard&quot;:3}" data-riff="ballad">

"Clavinet." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clavinet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clavinet). Pad, string and anvil, yarn damping, electromagnetic pickups; D6 (1971): Brilliant / Treble high-pass, Medium / Soft low-pass, AB and CD pickup rockers, mute slider; Use Me, Higher Ground.

"Pianet." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pianet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pianet). Pads lifting off reeds; N: leather pads, variable-capacitance pickup; T: suction pads, electromagnetic; models and years 1962-1983; vibrato switch, volume pedal; She's Not There, These Eyes.

"Rhodes Piano." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodes_piano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodes_piano). Tines, tonebar, pickup; Mark I Stage and Suitcase (1970), 73 keys, about 130 lb; the Suitcase's tremolo between two speakers labelled vibrato; recordings (Riders on the Storm, Angela).

"Wurlitzer Electronic Piano." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wurlitzer_electronic_piano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wurlitzer_electronic_piano). Felt hammer on a metal reed, electrostatic pickup at 170 V DC; 200 (1968, about 88,000), 200A (1974-1983), 64 keys, 56 lb, 30 W; single-speed vibrato; Supertramp and Queen.

"Yamaha CP-70." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yamaha_CP-70](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yamaha_CP-70). Hammers on strings, no soundboard, piezo pickups on the harp; CP-70 (1976, 73 keys), CP-80 (1978, 88), to 1985; short bass strings; Genesis, Peter Gabriel.
:::
